testerNoteNow:
Unchanged since 94b4f9238.

Local (NODE_ENV=development): what happens depends on your .env.
- With ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1, which scripts/setup-local-db.sh writes, password sign-in skips the code entirely.
- Otherwise, with SMTP unset, the code appears only as a debug-level JSON log line ("[email-service] Dev OTP code", field "code"). That line is hidden when LOG_LEVEL=info, which is what .env.example sets. If your .env was copied from .env.example, set LOG_LEVEL=debug or ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1. Otherwise you will wait on the code screen.
- If you do set SMTP locally, the code is emailed instead of logged. With SMTP_FROM left blank, it comes from noreply@concept2cure.pro.

Docker-compose stacks: both refuse to start unless SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS and SMTP_FROM are set (docker-compose.yml:219-223, docker-compose.beta.yml:221-225), so the .pro default never applies there. They only check that the values are present, not that they work.
- The send is not awaited. A wrong host, port or password, a sender address your provider will not send from (for example an unverified SES identity), or an SES-sandbox recipient fails after the screen has already said the code was sent. Resend says the same.
- The only trace is "Failed to send login OTP email" in the server log.
- If SMTP works but the sender domain has no SPF, DKIM or DMARC, the code can go to spam or be quarantined.

Workaround:
- Use a sender address on a domain verified with your SMTP provider.
- Before the session, run `node scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs <inbox>` once per tester inbox, from the repo root with the same .env the stack uses.
- Testers should check spam. Personal Gmail is more forgiving than corporate M365 gateways.
